title: The Dew Drop as hiring hall and hotel for visiting stars
summary: Musicians left messages and found gigs at the Dew Drop, where Ray Charles, Guitar Slim and Little Richard stayed.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: And $24 was damn good, too, you know. Sure. Yeah. $8 a night and 12. All you could drink. And so. So that's, and that's how they had operated. And they had comedians there, man. Uh, and all kinds of good shows. And musicians hung out there. Because, uh, in those days, we didn't have too many telephones at home. So if you wanted a bass player, a saxophone player, a drummer, anybody, a musician, or what and so forth and so on, most of the time, you give your number at the, at the doodrop. Uh-huh. So you want to pass that frequently and see if you got a message. Or if they call it in. Guys would hang around starting around 3 o'clock in the afternoon until 7 or 8 o'clock at night or so, just for, because if you wanted somebody, you called there. You got to a phone and you called the doodrop. Look, they got a bass player around there. You got a trumpet player around there. You know. I mean. And you got a gig. Yeah. Or you could go by there with your truck or station wagon, whatever you had. Uh-huh. And if you needed for three or four musicians to go on the gig, man, boom. They were there with the instruments. Uh-huh. And maybe have on a black shirt, black, uh, black suit and everything out ready to go. Pretty good. Because that's where you got your gigs from, you know.
Should they have, did they have like a bulletin board?
No. Or was it? Bulletin board was, I tell you, you tell him, you tell him. Or you go ask Frank.

Yeah. And you know, the people who stayed there at that time. Ray Charles, Guitar Slim. Yeah. Lil' Richard. Uh-huh. Dee Clark. If you came to town and you wanted to be where that was happening, you went to the Dewdrop.
